question.text: An existing mutual fund investor invests Rs. 25,000 through a distributor in a Regular Plan. Under the current NISM V-A workbook framework (post the August 2025 SEBI circular), what is the net amount invested in the scheme after accounting for transaction charges?

answer.text: Rs. 24,850 (after deducting Rs. 150 transaction charge for existing investors)
Rs. 24,900 (after deducting Rs. 100 transaction charge for existing investors)
Rs. 24,750 (after deducting Rs. 250 transaction charge for large investments)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the current NISM V-A workbook framework, SEBI has withdrawn the investor-borne transaction-charge benefit for mutual fund distributors. No transaction charge is deducted from investor contributions, so the full Rs. 25,000 is invested in the scheme. The Trap: The legacy Rs. 150 (new investor) / Rs. 100 (existing investor) split applied under the older framework and is now superseded. Rs. 250 is a fabricated combination figure. Cross-Exam Context: NISM V-A tests the withdrawal of upfront commissions and the investor-borne transaction-charge framework; distributor remuneration now flows through trail commissions and the additional-commission framework for new investors from B-30 cities and women investors as specified by SEBI.
